items.title: Data Breach Confirmed After Australian Energy Giant Origin Is Hacked
items.description: A hacker claims to have stolen the information of 2 million Origin Energy customers and is threatening to leak it. The post Data Breach Confirmed After Australian Energy Giant Origin Is Hacked appeared first on SecurityWeek.

items.title: Russian Hackers Exploit Zimbra Zero-Day Against US, Ukraine Targets
items.description: A state-sponsored threat group, dubbed "Laundry Bear," sends "half-click" phishing emails that require a victim only to open or preview the message.

items.title: New Dolphin X malware uses AI to rank high-value targets
items.description: A new Dolphin X remote access trojan claims to use an AI-powered profiling feature to score and rank infected users, helping cybercriminals identify which victims should be targeted first. [...]

items.title: Australian energy provider Origin says data breach exposes client data
items.description: Origin Energy has confirmed that an unauthorized party accessed and subsequently leaked customer data online, exposing sensitive personally identifiable information (PII), among others. [...]

items.title: Fake Claude app promoted by Bing ads pushes SectopRAT malware
items.description: A malvertising campaign on the Bing search service is pushing a fake Claude desktop app installer hosted on a legitimate Claude.ai domain to deliver the SectopRAT malware. [...]

items.title: Russian Espionage Group Exploited Zimbra Zero-Day to Steal Mail and 2FA Codes
items.description: A Russian state-supported espionage group spent months reading Western mailboxes through a then-unknown flaw in Zimbra's webmail client. The payload goes after the last 90 days of email, the organization's entire email directory, the password saved in the browser and the codes kept for two-factor recovery. items.title: Russian hackers exploit Zimbra zero-click flaw for email theft
items.description: CISA is warning that the Russian state-sponsored hacking group Laundry Bear, also known as Void Blizzard, is targeting organizations using Zimbra Collaboration email servers by combining phishing attacks with the exploitation of a now-patched Zimbra vulnerability. [...]

items.title: Hackers abuse Notepad++ plugins to stealthily install malware
items.description: Ukraine's CERT has uncovered attacks distributing an archive containing the legitimate Notepad++ application and a malicious utility called LunchPoke disguised as a plugin to establish persistence. [...]

items.title: OpenAI Fixes ChatGPT Agent Flaw That Could Let Attackers Forge an AI Insider
items.description: AgentForger allows an attacker to create, insert and remotely control an invisible autonomous AI agent inside a victim organization. The post OpenAI Fixes ChatGPT Agent Flaw That Could Let Attackers Forge an AI Insider appeared first on SecurityWeek.

items.title: Is Patching Dead? Vulnerability Management in the Post-Mythos Era
items.description: You cannot out-patch a machine that writes a working exploit from a vulnerability description in twenty hours. Stop trying to optimize a game you cannot win. The post Is Patching Dead? Vulnerability Management in the Post-Mythos Era appeared first on SecurityWeek.

items.title: Chick-fil-A Accounts Get Fried in Credential Stuffing Attack
items.description: Threat actors used credentials obtained from other companies to hack into Chick-fil-A One accounts. The post Chick-fil-A Accounts Get Fried in Credential Stuffing Attack appeared first on SecurityWeek.

items.title: Abstract Raises $25 Million to Expand Composable Security Operations Platform

items.title: Claude Cowork Flaw Could Let AI Agent Escape Its VM and Access Mac Files
items.description: Cybersecurity researchers have uncovered a sandbox escape vulnerability in Anthropic's Claude Cowork that makes it possible to break out of the confines of a Linux virtual machine (VM) within which the agent runs to read or write files anywhere on the Mac. items.title: Chaos Ransomware Uses msaRAT to Route C2 Traffic Through Headless Chrome and Edge
items.description: The Chaos ransomware group ran its command-and-control through the victim's own browser. Cisco Talos on Thursday detailed msaRAT, the Rust implant behind it, found on a compromised Windows machine ahead of the encryptor. The implant never opens an outbound connection of its own. items.title: Agentic AI Challenges Progress in Confidential Computing
items.description: Core issues that slowed down adoption of secure data vaults are being resolved by technology, but artificial intelligence poses new ones. Experts have some answers.

items.title: Brazilian Banking Trojan Actively Spreading in Portugal
